I have been farming this land in Iringa for many years, and I know what works. I will put some chemical fertilizer on this plot because the maize needs it to produce well, but money is tight so I can only buy a small amount. I also have cow manure that I will spread here, and I will use my own seed that I saved from last season because it is reliable and I do not have cash for the expensive hybrid seeds from town. My family will do most of the work by hand—weeding and harvesting this 0.63 hectare plot—but I will hire a few young men from the village when the weeding is heavy, since this plot is intercropped and there is much to do. We depend on the rains here in Iringa, so I will not irrigate, and I do not see the need for chemicals to kill pests when we can manage by hand.
